extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in NLP, formal methods, and autoformalization using LLMs (ML/NLP researchers, formal proof engineers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running evaluations that test how robust LLM-based autoformalization is to semantically similar paraphrases of natural-language statements, using formal benchmarks and measuring semantic and compilation-level outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure semantic validity of generated formalizations/proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated in the abstract: the paper evaluates robustness by "measuring semantic and compilation validity." Semantic validity here refers to whether the formalization preserves the meaning of the original natural-language statement (i.e., semantic fidelity between NL input and generated formal object). The page provides this high-level metric but not a formal definition on the landing page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure compilation validity of generated formal artifacts (whether the formalization/proof compiles in the proof assistant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract explicitly pairs "compilation validity" with semantic validity as an evaluation target. Compilation validity operationalizes whether the generated formal code/proof type-checks or compiles in the target formal system (e.g., Lean 4 ProofNet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to semantically similar paraphrasing (sensitivity to paraphrases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how small, semantically faithful paraphrases of the same NL statement affect model outputs and correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central claim evaluated is that LLMs can be sensitive to paraphrased NL inputs even when "high degrees of semantic fidelity are preserved." The methodology described on the page is to generate semantically similar paraphrases and measure resulting variability in model behavior; robustness is judged by stability of semantic and compilation validity across paraphrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance variability across paraphrased inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify variability in model performance (e.g., success rates for semantic/compilation validity) when the same underlying proposition is expressed with different paraphrases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract reports "performance variability across paraphrased inputs" as a core finding and thus treats variability itself as an evaluative metric: lower variability implies greater robustness. The landing page does not supply exact statistical measures but indicates measuring and reporting variability across paraphrases and models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-model cross-evaluation / consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-evaluate paraphrased statements across multiple LLMs to assess consistency and model-to-model differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors "generate paraphrased natural language statements and cross-evaluate these statements across both models." This implies a rubric dimension that looks at whether different models behave consistently on the same paraphrases and whether failures are model-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard formal benchmarks (MiniF2F and Lean 4 ProofNet)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate on established formal benchmarks to ground results: MiniF2F and the Lean 4 version of ProofNet are used as the formal problem suites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract specifies the benchmarks used: MiniF2F (Zheng, Han, and Polu 2021) and Lean 4 ProofNet (Xin et al. 2024). Inclusion of these benchmarks is a methodological/quality requirement for reproducibility and comparability: evaluations should use established datasets/benchmarks for formalization tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paraphrase generation method (preserve semantic fidelity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate paraphrases that preserve high degrees of semantic fidelity while varying surface form to probe model sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes creating "semantically similar paraphrased NL statements" as the input perturbations for testing. Though the landing page does not describe the paraphrase-generation algorithm, the implicit criterion is that paraphrases must be meaning-preserving (high semantic fidelity) so that differences in model output can be attributed to wording rather than meaning changes.
